newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia leading index rises in Oct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia leading index rises in Oct.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index of economic activity, which indicates where activity will be in six to nine months time, rose by 2.4 points or 1.7 percent in October, Westpac said on Wednesday.
It said the coincident index, which measures current activity, rose by 1.2 points or 0.7 percent in October.

The leading index of inflation was steady at 4.5 percent, with Westpac chief economist Nigel Stapledon saying in an accompanying statement that a fourth rate cut by the Reserve Bank of Australia is possible early next year.

Stapledon said the slow growth rate of the leading index suggests that economic activity will not have enough momentum to reverse the trend rise in unemployment until the second half of calendar 1997.

"The rise in the coincident index only partially redresses the sharp fall recorded in September and leaves the trend annual growth rate at just 0.1 percent. This reflects the present underlying weakness in the economy."

He said the Australian economy will achieve only a slow recovery in 1997, which endorsed the central bank's December 11 cut in the official cash rate to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent and which was supported by low inflation. This followed reductions of a similar size in late July and early November.

"The very positive short term outlook for inflation will be confirmed with the next set of inflation data due out in late January, which is likely to provide the backdrop to a possible fourth rate cut by the Reserve Bank," Stapledon said.
